 Early voting tops 51 million nationwide as turnout surges in key battlegrounds 
 Sana Azem 
 Updated: Oct 31, 2026 / 02:30 PM CDT 
 Comments: 
 NOW PLAYING
 Get fact-based,  unbiased political coverage  from the NewsNation team ahead of the 2026 elections.   Get 24/7 news coverage with the  NewsNation app. Not sure how to find NewsNation on your TV?   Find your channel here . And remember to sound off in the comments below!  
 ( NewsNation ) — More than 51 million Americans have voted early in person or returned mail ballots across the country, according to the Election Lab at the University of Florida .
 As of Saturday, more than 7 million people in Texas had voted early in person or returned mail ballots, according to the data. In Florida, more than 4 million people had voted early.
 Early voting is significantly outpacing the last midterm election, with millions more Americans casting ballots in advance and particularly sharp increases in states hosting competitive Senate races, according to an Associated Press analysis of voting data conducted five days before Election Day.
 Midterms are days away. Here’s what they usually mean for your money 
 Advance voting has increased by more than 30% compared with the same point four years ago in Maine, Michigan, North Carolina and Kansas, all states with competitive Senate races. In South Carolina, where voters are choosing a successor to the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, early voting is up 83%.
 Data from states with party registration show that more than 10 million registered Democrats have voted early, compared with more than 7 million registered Republicans, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.
 The Associated Press contributed to this report.
